BLA under FDA review 2026 — AD approval expected H1/H2 2026

Ph3 ADHERE: ~47% IGA 0/1 at Wk24 vs. 17% placebo. Q12W dosing is the headline differentiator vs. dupilumab Q2W. Anti-OX40L mechanism: blocks T-cell priming and Th2 memory cell amplification. Sanofi's own asset competing directly with Dupixent — validates OX40L as the next generation AD mechanism. If approved, validates OX40L as a target for IL-4Rα×OX40L bispecific positioning.

Ph3 data expected 2026. OX40 receptor blocking (vs. OX40L ligand blocking). Kaposi's sarcoma signal in predisposed patients; pyrexia/chills adverse events. Safety differentiation vs. OX40L: receptor blocking (rocatinlimab) may over-suppress T-cells vs. ligand blocking (amlitelimab, Ailux). Key read: if rocatinlimab shows efficacy with manageable safety, it confirms OX40 pathway is active in Ph3 — if safety issues emerge, further validates OX40L (ligand) approach.

OX40L+IL-4Rα/IL-13 trispecific. Ph2 positive data. First clinical validation of combining OX40L blockade with IL-4Rα pathway in a single molecule. Apogee does not have pH engineering. Watch: how does the combination signal separate vs. each arm alone?

Pure anti-OX40L monotherapy. Phase 1. Serves as a clean control for the OX40L mechanism contribution vs. APG279 combination. Key for understanding the additive/synergistic hypothesis of combining OX40L with IL-4Rα.

IL-4Rα × OX40L bispecific from China. Phase 1. Most direct format competitor to Ailux. No pH engineering; standard IgG scaffold. Confirms the bispecific target combination is moving through clinical development.
Ph3 pediatric. If Amlitelimab approved in adult AD + pediatric, OX40L blockade becomes a validated mechanism across the full AD patient spectrum, strengthening the bispecific combination thesis.
